correctness.rationale: Direct coefficientwise differentiation in characteristic 2 yields precisely the 3 displayed quadrics and Euler containment of the cubic. Their exact affine presentations on D(x0), D(x4), which cover J, are k[t,u]/u² and k[s,v]/v². Laurent transitions s=t^-1+t^-4u and v=t^-6u prove conormal O(-6) and the nonsplit obstruction t² in the Laurent quotient. The reduced support has codimension 3, hence the 3 quadrics are a regular sequence; adjunction and the nilradical sequence establish degree 8, genus 5, canonical embedding, and Hilbert polynomial. A standalone exact GF(2) verifier in the package replayed successfully. Proof contains the infinite-degree argument; experiments are supportive only.

originality.rationale: The precise 3x3 Hankel determinant is known from Raicu, while its secant geometry is known from Kanev; both pertinent full-text results are under characteristic-zero assumptions. Casalaina-Martin–Laza treats the complex chordal cubic as a degeneration, and Bayer–Eisenbud treats general ribbons without this explicit characteristic-2 Jacobian construction. Targeted mathematical-record queries and accessible earlier scientific claims do not cover the same characteristic-two full singular scheme, nilradical gluing and nonsplitting. value.rationale: The chordal cubic is a historically central cubic-threefold boundary. Its Jacobian singular scheme is a geometrically motivated invariant; in characteristic two it becomes a globally nonsplit canonical genus-five ribbon rather than just a reduced rational normal quartic. The computation determines full equations, a global obstruction class, genus, dualizing sheaf, and Hilbert polynomial. This contrasts with common reduced/char-zero descriptions and is not just a Jacobian derivative exercise.
